## [0.0.9] - 2026-11-23

### Changed

- The docs no longer promise source-contract features the plugin does not declare: `plaud.recordings` sends no `removals[]`, so a recording deleted after it was listed is not announced, and it does not declare `permission.readsIdentity`, so a page does not read who is signed in itself. The README and `docs/configuration.md` say so.
- `docs/jelly.md` names the pinned source contract, v0.3.0.
- The `opencode-plaud` skill lists the tools RPC methods correctly: the five reads, `recent`, `events_list`, `probe` and `describe`. `plaud_export` is not a method, so a script cannot export, and a script never gets a signed link.

No runtime change: the plugin's behaviour and its source declaration are unchanged.

### Known limits

- **Platforms.** macOS and Linux only. Windows is not tested.
- **Region.** Plaud's server is in the US. Accounts in other regions are untested; set `url` if Plaud gives you another address.
- **Read-only against Plaud.** Plaud has no write API, so nothing here creates, renames, deletes, uploads, shares or sends a recording.
- **New Plaud tools.** A tool Plaud adds later follows `access`, so it runs at the default `"all"`. It is not a script method until a plugin release.
- **Signed links.** Tool results never show a signed link. Audio and transcripts reach a file only through `plaud_export`.
- **Unattended exports.** An export folder is outside the project, so an unattended run needs the `external_directory` rule as well as `plaud_export` (see [Permissions](#permissions)).
- **Tested hosts.** Tested on OpenCode 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6, 2.2.7, 2.3.0, 2.3.1 and 2.3.2. A later 2.2 or 2.3 release starts, and `/plaud-status` marks it untested.
- **Other accounts in Jelly.** Jelly's declaration names another account's reads as patterns (`plaud-*.get_file` and the rest), so they keep their read-only rules in Jelly. In a Jelly that does not yet write a pattern's rules, those tools follow the plugin's namespace and are denied at Read only, reads included.
- **Jelly.** The settings declare their choices and bounds, which only a Jelly that includes app#1301 reads; an older Jelly refuses the plugin's declaration.
- **The recordings source.** `plaud.recordings` names the owner the account's last `probe` named, so every listing of an account, with a cursor or without, needs a probe of it since OpenCode started (`UNAVAILABLE` otherwise). A cursor issued for another Plaud user than the one the probe names is refused (`CURSOR_INVALID`). The plugin does not declare `permission.readsIdentity`: a page does not read who is signed in itself.
- **Other accounts through the source contract.** `plaud.recordings` declares `accounts.server` as `plaud-{account}`. A consumer's session rules for the default account allow `plaud_list_files` and `plaud_get_current_user`. For any other account they allow that account's server, `plaud-<alias>_list_files` and `plaud-<alias>_get_current_user`, which is what the plugin calls. A consumer still on source-contract `v0.1.x` refuses the `accounts.server` key and will not load this descriptor. Scripts and the model are unaffected.
- **Late uploads.** A device keeps its recordings until the Plaud app connects to it. A `recordings` page lists a recording that reached Plaud after the cursor passed its start if it started within the 14 days before the cursor (fewer when more recordings started then than the cursor can remember). One found in the 7 days before those with a `created_at` after the last page answers an `expired` gap, so a consumer lists again from its start; one that started earlier is not seen. Contract 1's `plaud` listing never lists a recording behind its cursor.
- **Deleted recordings.** A recording deleted in Plaud before a listing reaches it is not listed: it no longer exists, so no history is lost. A recording deleted after it was listed is not announced: the source does not send `removals[]`.

## [0.0.8] - 2026-11-20

### Added

- **List snapshot** `plaud.recordings.list` (`output: "list"`). An app can bind it and render recordings without
  knowing Plaud. It is the tools RPC method `events_list` with `{ "source": "recordings", "list": "recordings" }`; the
  model tool's schema has no `list`, so an agent sees no list. It calls the existing `list_files` read, not a second
  client, over the last 40 days and returns at most 50 recordings, newest first, each an id and a title; a title is
  screened whole and then cut to 200 characters, control characters are stripped, an id appears once, and the answer
  stops short of 256 KiB. `plaud.recordings` stays the events source and is not renamed, and no write is declared. Like
  it, the snapshot is a `named` source and declares `accounts.server` as `plaud-{account}`, so a consumer's session
  rules allow the server the account's reads actually call.

### Changed

- **Other accounts through the source contract.** `plaud.recordings` and `plaud.recordings.list` both declare
  `accounts.server` as `plaud-{account}`. A consumer's fenced session rules allow `plaud_list_files` and
  `plaud_get_current_user` for the default account, and `plaud-<alias>_list_files` and
  `plaud-<alias>_get_current_user` for any other, which is what the plugin calls. A consumer still on source-contract
  v0.1.x refuses the `accounts.server` key and will not load this descriptor. Scripts and the model are unaffected.
- Source contract `@we-the-rebel-alliance/source-contract` v0.3.0 (was v0.2.0), a devDependency bundled into `dist/`
  (no runtime dependency). The declaration and the probe answer are unchanged: the plugin sends none of v0.3.0's new
  keys (`facts`, `hints`, `routines`, an actor's `kind`, `sections` or `parts`), which a consumer still on v0.2.0
  refuses. The conformance test names the seven v0.3 checks the source carries nothing for, each with its reason.
- The docs now match the default rules: at `ask-changes` a Plaud tool added later asks, and a script cannot export,
  because `plaud_export` is not a tools RPC method.
- Jelly re-asks consent: `package.json`'s `sources` gains `plaud.recordings.list`, and `plaud.recordings` gains
  `accounts.server`.

### Known limits

- **Platforms.** macOS and Linux only. Windows is not tested.
- **Region.** Plaud's server is in the US. Accounts in other regions are untested; set `url` if Plaud gives you another address.
- **Read-only against Plaud.** Plaud has no write API, so nothing here creates, renames, deletes, uploads, shares or sends a recording.
- **New Plaud tools.** A tool Plaud adds later follows `access`, so it runs at the default `"all"`. It is not a script method until a plugin release.
- **Signed links.** Tool results never show a signed link. Audio and transcripts reach a file only through `plaud_export`.
- **Unattended exports.** An export folder is outside the project, so an unattended run needs the `external_directory` rule as well as `plaud_export` (see [Permissions](#permissions)).
- **Tested hosts.** Tested on OpenCode 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6, 2.2.7, 2.3.0, 2.3.1 and 2.3.2. A later 2.2 or 2.3 release starts, and `/plaud-status` marks it untested.
- **Other accounts in Jelly.** Jelly's declaration names another account's reads as patterns (`plaud-*.get_file` and the rest), so they keep their read-only rules in Jelly. In a Jelly that does not yet write a pattern's rules, those tools follow the plugin's namespace and are denied at Read only, reads included.
- **Jelly.** The settings declare their choices and bounds, which only a Jelly that includes app#1301 reads; an older Jelly refuses the plugin's declaration.
- **The recordings source.** `plaud.recordings` names the owner the account's last `probe` named, so every listing of an account, with a cursor or without, needs a probe of it since OpenCode started (`UNAVAILABLE` otherwise). A cursor issued for another Plaud user than the one the probe names is refused (`CURSOR_INVALID`).

## [0.0.6] - 2026-11-17

### Changed

- The source contract is `@we-the-rebel-alliance/source-contract` `v0.2.0` (it was `v0.1.0`), pinned to its tag and
  bundled into `dist/index.js`, so an install still has no runtime dependency. `plaud.recordings`, `events_list`,
  `probe` and their answers are unchanged: the plugin declares and sends none of `v0.2.0`'s new keys, which Memory and
  Jelly refuse until they read `v0.2.0` themselves.
- The conformance report is complete, and its `ok` is `true`: every check of the kit runs, the expired-gap checks
  (`gap-and-cursor-expired`, `gap-once-per-read`) included, except `failed-holds-cursor`, which cannot apply to this
  source and says why in the report (`atomicPages`, as before: `list_files` answers whole pages and no recording is read
  on its own, so none can fail alone). `npm run conformance` runs the conformance test alone and writes
  `reports/conformance-report.json`.
- A recording deleted in Plaud before a listing reaches it is not listed, and is not lost history: it no longer exists.
  Once Memory and Jelly read source-contract `v0.2.0`, a recording deleted after it was listed will be announced in the
  page's `removals[]`; until then the plugin sends no `removals[]`.
- Releases use the family's release kit r4.1: a release runs `npm run conformance` on its parent in a job of its own,
  with no write token, stops unless the report is `ok` for its version, and attaches it as the Release asset
  `conformance-report.json`, listed in `SHA256SUMS`; the tarball the pack job keeps is checked by its sha256 after every
  download. `docs/jelly.md` carries Jelly's shared paragraph on tools and permissions, and the declaration test knows
  Jelly's `cost` and `admin` lines.
- CI run by hand (`workflow_dispatch`) has its own concurrency group, so it never cancels a push run on `master`.
- Tested on OpenCode 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6, 2.2.7 and 2.3.0; the host range is still `>=2.2.3 <2.4.0`.

### Fixed

- `recordings` no longer skips a recording that reaches Plaud late. A device keeps its recordings until the Plaud app
  connects to it, so a recording can reach Plaud hours or days after it started, once the cursor has passed its start;
  the cursor only moved forward, so such a recording was never listed. A `recordings` page now reads again the 14 days
  before its cursor and lists every recording there the cursor has not listed: the cursor keeps a 24-bit digest of each
  recording it listed in those days (as many as fit the contract's 1,024 characters; with more, its lookback is shorter),
  the time its page was read, and where its lookback starts. A recording that reached Plaud later than that, found in the
  7 days before the lookback with a `created_at` after the last page was read, makes the page answer
  `gap: { reason: "expired", since }` from its start, once per read: a consumer lists again from `since`. One that
  started before those 7 days is not seen. Each listing now reads at least three weeks of `list_files`. A cursor from
  0.0.5 is still accepted, and lists on from its position. The default source `plaud` is unchanged.

### Known limits

- **Platforms.** macOS and Linux only. Windows is not tested.
- **Region.** Plaud's server is in the US. Accounts in other regions are untested; set `url` if Plaud gives you another address.
- **Read-only against Plaud.** Plaud has no write API, so nothing here creates, renames, deletes, uploads, shares or sends a recording.
- **New Plaud tools.** A tool Plaud adds later follows `access`, so it runs at the default `"all"`. It is not a script method until a plugin release.
- **Signed links.** Tool results never show a signed link. Audio and transcripts reach a file only through `plaud_export`.
- **Unattended exports.** An export folder is outside the project, so an unattended run needs the `external_directory` rule as well as `plaud_export` (see [Permissions](#permissions)).
- **Tested hosts.** Tested on OpenCode 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6,

## [0.0.5] - 2026-11-15

### Changed

- The icon is now Plaud's own mark, Plaud's arch symbol on a white tile, as in Plaud's own app icon, in place of the family's drawn mark; `opencode.vendor.mark` is `true`, and the README says Plaud is a trademark of PLAUD LLC.

### Known limits

- **Platforms.** macOS and Linux only. Windows is not tested.
- **Region.** Plaud's server is in the US. Accounts in other regions are untested; set `url` if Plaud gives you another address.
- **Read-only against Plaud.** Plaud has no write API, so nothing here creates, renames, deletes, uploads, shares or sends a recording.
- **New Plaud tools.** A tool Plaud adds later follows `access`, so it runs at the default `"all"`. It is not a script method until a plugin release.
- **Signed links.** Tool results never show a signed link. Audio and transcripts reach a file only through `plaud_export`.
- **Unattended exports.** An export folder is outside the project, so an unattended run needs the `external_directory` rule as well as `plaud_export` (see [Permissions](#permissions)).
- **Tested hosts.** Tested on OpenCode 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6, 2.2.7 and 2.3.0. A later 2.2 or 2.3 release starts, and `/plaud-status` marks it untested.
- **Other accounts in Jelly.** Jelly's declaration names another account's reads as patterns (`plaud-*.get_file` and the rest), so they keep their read-only rules in Jelly. In a Jelly that does not yet write a pattern's rules, those tools follow the plugin's namespace and are denied at Read only, reads included.
- **Jelly.** The settings declare their choices and bounds, which only a Jelly that includes app#1301 reads; an older Jelly refuses the plugin's declaration.
- **The recordings source.** `plaud.recordings` names the owner the account's last `probe` named, so every listing of an account, with a cursor or without, needs a probe of it since OpenCode started (`UNAVAILABLE` otherwise). A cursor issued for another Plaud user than the one the probe names is refused (`CURSOR_INVALID`). The source contract `v0.1.0` does not let a page read who is signed in itself (source-contract#30).
- **Other accounts through the source contract.** The source contract `v0.1.0` derives a consumer's session rules for `plaud.recordings` as `plaud_get_current_user` and `plaud_list_files`, whatever the account, while another account's reads are its own server's, `plaud-<alias>_…`. So a consumer's fenced read of an account other than `default` is refused by the session until the contract can name a per-account server. Scripts and the model are unaffected.
- **A day's query spans three days.** Plaud's date filter takes whole days (`YYYY-MM-DD`) in a time zone its docs do not name, so the plugin's narrowest query asks for a day and one either side. While Plaud ignores `page` under a date filter, three days that hold more recordings than one page of Plaud's answer keep failing with `PLAUD_READ_FAILED` (the cursor stays put, so nothing is lost) until Plaud honours `page`, or until such a listing is started after those days.
- **Plaud's limits.** Plaud publishes no request limit for its server, and its docs say `list_files` ignores `page` and `page_size` under a date filter, which `events_list` always sets. So when a page that is not empty repeats the one before, whatever its length, the plugin cannot tell whether Plaud sent every recording, and lists the week again one day at a time; when a day's query still repeats, it fails with `PLAUD_READ_FAILED` before the cursor moves, rather than skip a recording ([Plaud MCP](https://docs.plaud.ai/plaud-mcp-cli/mcp), "Filtering recordings with `list_files`"). The source's answers in the conformance test are invented in the shapes those docs give, not recorded from a live account.
- Updates are not automatic for a Git install, and `opencode plugin update` and `opencode plugin check` do not work on one: to move to a newer release, remove the old entry and add the new tag.
